1. Clean 7/7 Verified Hook Engine: removed 3 uncalled ColorOS 17 hooks (getAccelerateScale, isReduceDisabled, getLargeChangeLimit) verified as zero-hit over 24h runtime telemetry, numbered all settings toggles (#1–#7), and added a complete 7-hook reference card right below.\n2. Vector Framework & LibXposed API 102 priority: native XposedService + RemotePreferences sync allows instant zero-root settings updates while preserving full SystemProperties fallback for legacy LSPosed forks.\n3. Persistent ring log & accurate statistics: GUARD_STATS telemetry + persistent disk log (/data/system/autobrightness_guard.log), burst-coalesced counters, 10 lx Aux deadband filtering, ColorOS 17 calibration, and unified OLED/Light M3 UI.
What is the OxygenOS / ColorOS auto-brightness bug?

On OnePlus / OPPO devices (OxygenOS / ColorOS 12–17), OplusAutomaticBrightnessController schedules an AlarmManager timer (usually 10 minutes) when the screen turns off. When triggered, resetAutoBrightness() (or resetAutoBrightness(1) with DragOpt on ColorOS 17) and OplusBrightnessAmbientAdapter.resetAmbientAdapter("AutoReset") erase your learned brightness curve.
How do Vector Framework and KSUN + SUSFS work together?

This module communicates with Vector Framework directly via Binder (LibXposed RemotePreferences & XposedService) for live settings and scope status without calling su. Root access (KSUN, Magisk, APatch) is only needed inside the app when reading log files, dumpsys display panel calibration, or running Soft Reboot — compatible with SUSFS hiding.
Is a reboot required after updating or changing settings?

Changing toggles, minimum floor, sensor switches, or custom curve points applies INSTANTLY with zero reboot. Only upgrading the module APK (when hook code changes inside system_server) requires a 5-second Soft Reboot (available in Tools) or full reboot.
Does the module increase battery drain?

No. Hardware light sensors and brightness observers register strictly while the app is open on screen (ON_RESUME / ON_PAUSE). Disabled sensors (MAIN / AUX / PWM) unsubscribe completely. Inside system_server, all 7 hooks run with zero background threads or timers, burst-coalesced telemetry, and at most one GUARD_STATS write per 60 seconds.
How each hook inside system_server works and where to configure it

Intercepts both variants (including ColorOS 17 DragOpt resetAutoBrightness(1)). Blocks only screen-off sleep timer resets (lambda$new$1 or AlarmManager$ListenerWrapper stack). Turning auto-brightness off/on manually passes undisturbed. Controlled in Settings [Hook #1].

Blocks sleep-timer resets of the ambient lux interpolation adapter (reason="AutoReset", "resetAutoBrightness", or AlarmManager stack) so adaptive spline memory survives screen-off standby. Controlled in Settings [Hook #2].

Suppresses background micro-adjustments (RecoverChange / StableForceChange) that cause brightness to drift upward or downward while sitting under constant room lighting. Controlled in Settings [Hook #3].

Dual sub-hook: 4a disables hidden 20-minute progressive dimming in dark rooms; 4b enforces either an automatic 8.5 nit night floor (auto-brightness only, paused while dragging the slider) or an unconditional 1–150 nit manual floor across all apps. Controlled in Settings [Hook #4].

Filters indoor rear light sensor spikes when auxLux exceeds mainLux by >10 lx and >1.15x (blending 60% toward auxLux + 0.35 EMA smoothing below 200 lx; unfiltered above 200 lx outdoors). Also executes MAIN and AUX sensor disable toggles from Overview. Controlled in Settings [Hook #5] & Overview.

Samples the device\'s real stock ROM spline (STOCK_CURVE) and, when Custom Curve is enabled, substitutes your 7-point log-lux to nit curve (0–10,000 lx) in real time without reboot; above 10,000 lx yields to stock HBM/sunlight peak if higher. Controlled on Overview → Curve Editor.

Caches high_pwm_rgb (tcs3720) sensor handles inside system_server with zero allocation and drops its event stream when toggled OFF on Overview, stopping high-frequency under-display PWM readings when undesired. Controlled on Overview → Brightness & Sensors [PWM • #7].
